record.paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
record.context_brief: Iterative roots of complex cubic polynomials
record.original_question: Determine whether every complex polynomial of degree 3 has a polynomial square iterative root. In other words, for every complex cubic polynomial f, decide whether there always exists a complex polynomial φ such that φ(φ(z)) = f(z) for all complex z.

evidence.quote: In fact, even iterative roots of polynomials are not described. Even worse: we do not know whether every complex cubic polynomial has a square root.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f: ℂ → ℂ be a polynomial of degree 3 with complex coefficients. A polynomial square iterative root of f is a polynomial φ ∈ ℂ[z] satisfying the functional equation
   φ(φ(z)) = f(z)   for all z ∈ ℂ.
Determine whether for every complex cubic polynomial f there exists such a polynomial φ. Equivalently, decide whether the class of complex polynomials of degree 3 is contained in the image of the second iterate map P ↦ P∘P on ℂ[z].
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of describing which polynomials admit polynomial iterative square roots has only been completely settled for low degrees: Rice–Schweizer–Sklar (1980) characterized quadratics (none have a polynomial square root), and Schweizer–Sklar (1988) treated certain quartic cases. Subsequent works (e.g., Zhang–Yang and others, including a SCienceDirect article "Discussion on polynomials having polynomial iterative roots") discuss cubic iterative roots of polynomial form but do not provide a full characterization for degree-3 targets. No source found in the search resolves whether every complex cubic polynomial admits a polynomial square iterative root; the question is consistently stated as open.

status_evidence.title: When is f(f(z)) = az^2+bz+c? — Rice, Schweizer, Sklar
status_evidence.snippet: Classical result showing no quadratic polynomial is a second iterate of a polynomial.
status_evidence.claim: Only the quadratic case is fully resolved in the negative; higher-degree analogues remained open.

status_evidence.title: Discussion on polynomials having polynomial iterative roots
status_evidence.snippet: Up to now only roots of quadratic polynomial form are fully discussed; cubic iterative roots are studied partially.
status_evidence.claim: A complete description for cubic polynomials having polynomial iterative square roots is not available.
